1.explanation:
The heart of the duplication lives in the TreeSelect implementation itself.  

• src/tree-select/tree-select.jsx  
  – This is where the component reads `props.value` (or `defaultValue`) and maps each entry to a rendered “tag” inside the input box.  The current logic can push the same item multiple times (especially when disabled items are picked) and it uses the non‐unique `value` as the React `key`.  

• src/tree-select/index.jsx  
  – This file wires up the TreeSelect and its static `Node` sub‐component.  While it does not contain the tag‐rendering logic, any fix in `tree-select.jsx` must be correctly exported through this entry point.  

To fix the bug you’ll need to:
1. Dedupe the list of items before you render tags (so each value only produces one tag).  
2. Use a truly unique key (for example the internally generated `pos` or an explicit `key` prop on each data item) instead of the raw `value` string.  

Both of those changes happen in `src/tree-select/tree-select.jsx`, and the corrected component is then re‐exported via `src/tree-select/index.jsx`.
1.bug_scenario:
When you use a controlled TreeSelect in “checkbox‐mode” (treeCheckable) and you pass in a default value array that includes disabled leaf nodes, on mount the component will render each selected label multiple times in the input box and you will see a React key‐duplication warning:

• You set `treeDefaultExpandAll` + `treeCheckable` + `value={['4','6']}` where node “4” is disabled.  
• On initial render you get four “Input” tags (instead of one) and a console warning: “Encountered two children with the same key, ‘4’.”  

This happens because the code that turns your `value` array into tag elements is inadvertently producing duplicate entries (and using the `value` string as the React `key`).

2.explanation: Both of these files control how TreeSelect builds its UI and render the list of selected items (tags) in the input. index.jsx wires up props and exports the component, but the core tag‐rendering logic lives in tree-select.jsx. In tree-select.jsx there’s a loop over the selected values that constructs Tag (span) elements, using the node’s value as the key. Because disabled nodes are still present in the internal checked array and the value array, the same value appears twice, so you get duplicate tags and duplicate React keys. Fixing this requires deduplicating values or generating a truly unique key (for example combining value with its tree position) when mapping to tags in tree-select.jsx.
2.bug_scenario: When TreeSelect is used in checkbox‐multiple mode (treeCheckable) with a defaultValue that includes disabled leaf nodes, the initial rendering of selected tags in the input duplicates the same label multiple times and triggers a React “duplicate key” warning. In the screenshot you can see “Input ×” rendered four times for a single selected node, and the console warns “Encountered two children with the same key, ‘4’ …”. This happens because TreeSelect maps selected values directly to Tag (span) elements using the node’s value as the React key, and disabled nodes or strict‐check logic can end up contributing the same key twice.
